cards.quote: From 1994 to 1997, he donned the Troy Trojans jersey, leaving an indelible mark on the NCAA Division I men's basketball league. As a freshman, Rhodney burst onto the scene, showcasing his impressive skills and athleticism. His 6'5" frame and lightning-quick reflexes made him a force to be reckoned with on the court. In his inaugural season, he averaged 12.5 points per game, earning him a spot on the Atlantic Sun Conference's All-Freshman Team. This impressive debut set the tone for a remarkable collegiate career. During his sophomore year, Rhodney continued to dominate, leading the Trojans to a 20-win season and a berth in the Atlantic Sun Conference Tournament championship game. His 17.2 points per game average earned him a spot on the All-Conference First Team, solidifying his position as one of the top players in the league. As Rhodney entered his junior year, he was poised to take his game to new heights. And he did just that, guiding the Trojans to a 22-win season and a second consecutive appearance in the Atlantic Sun Conference Tournament championship game. His impressive stats – 19.5 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game – earned him a nod as a Mid-Major All-American. Rhodney's senior year was a testament to his growth and dedication. He led the Trojans to a 25-win season, the best in program history at the time, and a third consecutive appearance in the Atlantic Sun Conference Tournament championship game. His remarkable 21.1 points per game average earned him a spot on the All-Conference First Team for the third consecutive year. Throughout his four-year tenure, Rhodney Donaldson played in 114 games, starting in 104 of them. He scored a total of 1,934 points, averaging 17.0 points per game, and grabbed 744 rebounds, averaging 6.5 per game. His impressive stats and accolades are a testament to his hard work and dedication to the sport. Rhodney's remarkable collegiate career is a shining example of his participation in the NCAA Division I men's basketball league.
